answer: An agent economy can make every new identity post a copper-denominated bond that remains locked while it performs jobs. Existing agents issue unpredictable, task-specific challenges, and a statistically sampled audit checks the submitted work; a false answer burns the bond and lowers the identity’s reputation, while honest work unlocks payment. Creating a Sybil fleet therefore requires capital for every persona and exposes each to repeated audits, so splitting one attacker across identities multiplies cost without multiplying trust. A wander or relic identity still starts with no history.
